featureRef: 18.9 Recording maintenance or a change of condition
name: Record servicing, repair and condition against an asset, with what it cost
priorityReason: A verification and a disposal both read this history, and neither can be judged without it.

goal.capability: to record what was done to an asset, what it cost, and what condition it is in now
goal.outcome: the school can see what an asset has cost it since purchase and what state it is in

secondaryActors.involvement: Records the cost and posts it to the ledger.

externalActors.involvement: Carries out the servicing or repair. Holds no login.

additional.description: A physical verification finds an asset broken, which is resolved by a maintenance record.

preconditions.condition: The asset is on the register.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Staff or Accounts.
A voucher can be raised where there is a cost.

establishedBy.name: Accounting vouchers for money in and out

postConditions: The maintenance, servicing or repair is recorded against the asset with its date and its supplier.
Any cost was recorded and posted to the ledger through the ordinary voucher route.
The asset's condition was updated to what it is now.
The history stays on the asset and is visible when it is verified or disposed of.
What the asset has cost the school since purchase can be read from the register.
An asset whose condition fell to unserviceable is visible as a candidate for disposal.
Nothing was deleted. A record entered wrongly is corrected by a further record.

businessRules.rule: Maintenance, servicing or a repair is recorded against the asset with the date and the supplier. A record with no date and no supplier cannot be checked against an invoice.
The cost is recorded and posted through the ordinary voucher route for money leaving the school. No separate mechanism exists.
The asset's condition is updated by the record. The register shows what the asset is like now rather than what it was like when it was bought.
A condition may be changed without any work being done — an asset found damaged, or degraded through use — and is recorded as a condition change with no supplier and no cost.
The history stays on the asset and is visible when it is verified or disposed of. A disposal judged without knowing what has already been spent on the thing is a decision made blind.
The total maintenance cost since purchase is shown on the asset, so an asset costing more to keep than to replace is visible.
A maintenance record is never deleted or edited. A record entered wrongly is corrected by a further record, so the history stays a history.
Maintenance cannot be recorded against an asset that has been disposed of.
An asset whose condition falls to unserviceable is visible as a candidate for disposal, but nothing disposes of it automatically. Disposal is its own decision with its own approval.

outOfScope.item: Scheduling preventive maintenance in advance, which is not modelled

handledBy.name: Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals

departures.requirement: A maintenance record is never edited or deleted. A wrong record is corrected by a further one, so the history stays a history.
The register always shows the asset's present condition, not the condition it was in when bought.
A recorded cost above zero always raises a voucher and posts to the ledger. There is no route that records a cost the books never see.
No asset is retired by its condition. Disposal is a separate decision with its own approval.
Maintenance records are retained 7 years after the asset is disposed of.

openQuestions.question: Is preventive maintenance scheduled anywhere, or is every record entered after the fact?
openQuestions.assumption: After the fact as modelled. Nothing schedules a service.

openQuestions.question: Does maintenance cost affect the asset's book value, or is it expensed?
openQuestions.assumption: Expensed as modelled. Nothing capitalises it, and nothing calculates a book value at all.

openQuestions.question: Should an asset costing more in maintenance than it cost to buy be flagged automatically?
openQuestions.assumption: The figures are shown but nothing flags it.

openQuestions.question: Who is the supplier, given no feature creates a supplier record?
openQuestions.assumption: Typed each time. The document names this as a missing structure.

openQuestions.question: Should a condition change require any approval, given it can make an asset a disposal candidate?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
